Plot the bootstrap-assessed edges of an htna network

Source: R/plot_htna_bootstrap.R
plot_htna_bootstrap.Rd

plot_htna_bootstrap() plots the bootstrap-assessed edges of an htna network: it shows which transitions of a heterogeneous network are stable enough to interpret. Edges that are significant across resamples are drawn solid, the others dashed (or hidden), so the reader sees which within-actor transitions and which hand-overs between actors the data support. A bootstrap of a transition network resamples the sessions many times and records how often each edge is present and how much its weight varies.

plot_htna_bootstrap() draws the result of bootstrap_htna() in the layout and actor styling of plot_htna(). With display = "significant" only the significant edges are drawn; show_ci = TRUE adds the confidence interval of each edge weight. A grouped bootstrap is drawn as one plot per cohort, titled with its cohort name. plot() on a bootstrap result calls this function. It is called for the plot and returns, invisibly, the value of the drawing call, or boot for a grouped bootstrap.

The table behind the plot (one row per edge, with its weight, interval and p-value) is returned by summary() of the bootstrap result.

Usage

plot_htna_bootstrap(boot, group_colors = htna_palette, ...)

# S3 method for class 'htna_bootstrap'
plot(x, ...)

Arguments

boot, x

A result of bootstrap_htna(): an htna_bootstrap or an htna_bootstrap_group.

group_colors

Colours of the actor types, in actor order. Default htna_palette.

...

Further drawing arguments: display ("styled" (default), "significant" or "full"), show_ci (default FALSE), show_stars (default TRUE), title, and the arguments of cograph::splot().

Value

Called for the plot. Invisibly, the value of the drawing call for one bootstrap, or boot for a grouped bootstrap.

Conditions

htna_empty_input for a grouped bootstrap without cohorts; htna_bad_input when boot is not a result of bootstrap_htna() on an htna network.

See also

bootstrap_htna(), plot_htna(), certainty_htna()

Examples

data(human_ai)
net  <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (42 sessions), 'actor_type' (24 sessions)
boot <- bootstrap_htna(net, iter = 50, seed = 1)
plot_htna_bootstrap(boot)

plot_htna_bootstrap(boot, display = "significant")
